title: John catena: In the beginning was the Word (opening frag.)
english: Setting him forth as craftsman of all things, the name ‘Word’ is predicated of him.

For since, as a rule, every work of crafting depends on a word, there was no other way to declare him maker of all — for those who possess it (and this is a productive state joined with guileless reason).
But the Son of God, being none other than the craftsman of wisdom and art, is fittingly named ‘Word.’
For it is not some other substance, distinct from the Word, that makes existing things through him; he himself is the maker, being God the Word.
Then, since this Word — being God in substance and being in himself the Son of God — became man for the sake of human salvation, the Word was named ‘Flesh.’

And since some, having fallen from right faith, suppose that he exists only from the time when he came forth having become man from the virgin, the theologian most rightly writes against such people: [[In the beginning was the Word >> Bible:John 1:1]].
And using the verbs fittingly, by ‘became’ he signifies his flesh, and by ‘was’ his Godhead.

It would have been more proper to say ‘is’ of the Word of God; but since he was declaring the Word’s existence by way of distinguishing the incarnation, which happened at a certain time, the evangelist used ‘was’ instead of ‘is.’

But one must not take the proper significations of verbs when they are applied to eternal things; for it is when the things signified by them have an existence measured by time that ‘was’ means what is no longer but once was — just as ‘is’ signifies what now exists, as ‘will be’ what is going to exist.
But since the Word of God is eternal… [the fragment breaks off]

title: John catena: witnesses and the Baptist’s voice
english: And ‘[[he dwelt among us >> Bible:John 1:14]]’ — and this very name it bore, ‘God with us’ — but when he created, since it was not as a man sent by the Father that he brought all things into being: ‘he was with God, and was God.’

The Son of God is also called ‘Wisdom,’ created as ‘beginning of God’s ways’ according to the writing of Proverbs — because God’s Wisdom, existing in relation to him whose Wisdom she is, had no relation to anything else, but by God’s good pleasure willed that the creatures should come into being.

This Wisdom, then, willed to take up a creative relation to the things that were to be; and this is what is signified by her being created ‘beginning of God’s ways’ — along which ways he traverses, ordering beings, exercising providence, doing good, bestowing grace, in this Wisdom who was created.

They say, then, that the Word is ‘beginning’ — not being other than her in substance, but in our conception and in relation — so that it is the same existence which the scriptures now name in respect of substance: Wisdom insofar as she has been made God’s own, and the creative Word insofar as he has inclined, so to speak, toward the things made.

But it is not only here that the Son of God is called ‘Word’; sayings can be set alongside not only from the New Testament but also from the Old: ‘[[By the word of the Lord the heavens were established >> Bible:Psalm 33:6]]’; and ‘[[He sent his word and healed them >> Bible:Psalm 107:20]]’; and Luke… [the fragment breaks off]
